description: Official West Coast Charts MCP server: render, validate and describe charts headlessly (SVG/PNG + verification table), option schema slices and curated examples for AI agents.
instructions:
West Coast Charts: render, validate and describe charts (ApexCharts-compatible JSON options) headlessly.
Workflow: list_chart_types -> list_examples/get_example -> get_schema for unsure options -> validate_chart until ok -> render_chart -> check the verification table.
All tools are read-only and deterministic. Errors are isError results {error:{kind,message,hint,details}}; follow the hint. Premium types need a licence key (kind "license", details.reason license_required|license_invalid). Verification tables use the wcc-describe/1 shape.
Docs: resource wcc://docs/agent-quickstart.

tools.name: render_chart
tools.title: Render chart (SVG/PNG + verification table)
tools.description:
Render a West Coast Charts spec headlessly to SVG or PNG and return the image together with the verification table: the values, aggregates and text description that were actually drawn.
Use it to produce a chart file or to check that a chart shows what you intended. Read the returned table instead of looking at the image when you cannot see images. Do not use it just to check option names (validate_chart is faster) or only for the numbers (describe_chart is cheaper).
Behaviour: read-only, deterministic (same spec+seed => byte-identical output, animations off), no files written, no network. The spec is validated first (validate: "strict" rejects invalid options with kind "schema" and fix hints; "warn" renders anyway and lists warnings).
Premium types (sankey, chord, gantt, tree, stock, map, marimekko, network, radialColumn) need a licence key on the server; without one the call fails with kind "license" (details.reason "license_required"), unless the server runs with --evaluation (WCC_EVALUATION=1): then they render with an "unlicensed" watermark.
Example: {"spec": {"chart":{"type":"bar"},"series":[{"name":"Revenue","data":[12,19,7]}],"xaxis":{"categories":["Q1","Q2","Q3"]}}, "format": "svg"}

series.description: Data series, ApexCharts-compatible shape (array of {name, data} or numbers for pie/donut/radialBar). Omit when `data` is given.

spec.description: West Coast Charts options object, JSON only (no functions), the same object you pass to new WestCoastCharts(el, options). ApexCharts 4.x options are accepted. Example: {"chart":{"type":"bar"},"series":[{"name":"Revenue","data":[12,19,7]}],"xaxis":{"categories":["Q1","Q2","Q3"]}}

data.description: Optional series array that replaces spec.series (keeps the spec reusable as a template).

format.description: Output format. svg (default) is text and editable; png is a base64 image.

width.description: Canvas width in px. Default spec.chart.width or 800.

height.description: Canvas height in px. Default spec.chart.height or 450.

theme.description: Theme. Default spec.theme.mode or the server default.

seed.description: Random seed for layouts (network, facets). Same spec + seed => byte-identical output. Default 1.

scale.description: PNG pixel ratio 1-4. Default 1. Ignored for svg.

background.description: CSS colour behind the chart. PNG default '#ffffff'; SVG stays transparent unless set.

validate.description: Run validate_chart first. strict (default) fails on errors, warn renders and reports, off skips.

delivery.description: inline (default) embeds the SVG text/PNG bytes; link returns only a resource link wcc://renders/{id} plus the table (saves tokens; read the resource when needed).

uri.description: wcc://renders/{id} resource with the rendered file

text.description: accessible text description of what was drawn (the chart's <desc>)

rows.description: cells are formatted strings, as displayed

table.description: the data table as drawn (same as the chart’s accessible data table)

series.description: per series: count, min/max point, unit, aggregate

aggregate.description: chart-level combined value with its function (e.g. p95 latencies: max, never sum)

table.description: Verification table (wcc-describe/1): text, table {caption, columns, rows (strings), total, truncated}, aggregate, series...

tableSource.description: where the table came from: 'describe' = full E2 model from chart.describe(); 'stub' = basic table extracted from the drawn chart (no per-series aggregates, scales or marks); null = no table

meta.description: {type, premium, licensed, licenseKeySource, width, height, seed, tableSource, libVersion, renderCoreVersion, fontSet, ms, warnings}

tools.name: validate_chart
tools.title: Validate chart spec
tools.description:
Check a West Coast Charts spec without rendering. Returns structured issues, each with a stable code, the dotted option path, a message, a hint with the exact fix and, for typos or invented options, the suggested correct key (did-you-mean).
Use it before render_chart when you wrote options from memory, and after every fix until ok is true. An invalid spec is a normal result (ok:false), not a tool error. It does not check whether the data makes sense; use describe_chart for that.
Read-only, deterministic, fast (no rendering).
Example: {"spec": {"chart": {"type": "radialColumn"}, "plotOptions": {"radialColumn": {"agregate": "max"}}}} -> error WCC_UNKNOWN_OPTION at plotOptions.radialColumn.agregate, suggestion "aggregate".

series.description: Data series, ApexCharts-compatible shape (array of {name, data} or numbers for pie/donut/radialBar). Omit when `data` is given.

spec.description: West Coast Charts options object, JSON only (no functions), the same object you pass to new WestCoastCharts(el, options). ApexCharts 4.x options are accepted. Example: {"chart":{"type":"bar"},"series":[{"name":"Revenue","data":[12,19,7]}],"xaxis":{"categories":["Q1","Q2","Q3"]}}

data.description: Optional series array that replaces spec.series (keeps the spec reusable as a template).

errors.description: Issue[] {code, path, message, hint, suggestion, severity:"error"}

validator.description: 'e1' matching released library validator; no approximate fallback

tools.name: describe_chart
tools.title: Describe chart (verification table)
tools.description:
Return the verification table (wcc-describe/1) of a spec without producing an image: the text description, the data table as drawn (caption, columns, rows of formatted strings, total, truncated) and, from the full model, per-series and chart-level aggregates with their function (sum/mean/max/min/none), scales, extrema and hidden series. Aggregates follow the chart's semantics, e.g. p95 latencies are reported as a maximum, never summed.
Use it to check, in text only, that a chart says what you intend, to write alt text, or to answer questions about a chart. Cheaper than render_chart; use render_chart instead when you need the image.
Read-only and deterministic.
Example: {"spec": {"chart":{"type":"bar"},"series":[{"name":"Revenue","data":[12,19,7]}],"xaxis":{"categories":["Q1","Q2","Q3"]}}, "format": "markdown"}

series.description: Data series, ApexCharts-compatible shape (array of {name, data} or numbers for pie/donut/radialBar). Omit when `data` is given.

spec.description: West Coast Charts options object, JSON only (no functions), the same object you pass to new WestCoastCharts(el, options). ApexCharts 4.x options are accepted. Example: {"chart":{"type":"bar"},"series":[{"name":"Revenue","data":[12,19,7]}],"xaxis":{"categories":["Q1","Q2","Q3"]}}

data.description: Optional series array that replaces spec.series (keeps the spec reusable as a template).

format.description: markdown (default): text + table + aggregates; json: the wcc-describe/1 object, then a second text item with the table source (both also in structuredContent.table / .tableSource).

max_rows.description: Rows shown in markdown output. Default 50. json returns every row the core returned (see table.total/truncated).

width.description: Canvas width in px. Default spec.chart.width or 800.

height.description: Canvas height in px. Default spec.chart.height or 450.

theme.description: Theme. Default spec.theme.mode or the server default.

seed.description: Random seed for layouts (network, facets). Same spec + seed => byte-identical output. Default 1.

text.description: accessible text description of what was drawn (the chart's <desc>)

rows.description: cells are formatted strings, as displayed

table.description: the data table as drawn (same as the chart’s accessible data table)

series.description: per series: count, min/max point, unit, aggregate

aggregate.description: chart-level combined value with its function (e.g. p95 latencies: max, never sum)

tableSource.description: where the table came from: 'describe' = full E2 model from chart.describe(); 'stub' = basic table extracted from the drawn chart (no per-series aggregates, scales or marks); null = no table

tools.name: get_schema
tools.title: Get option schema slice
tools.description:
Return the JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of West Coast Charts options, either the root or the slice at a dotted path. Deeper levels are collapsed to stubs with "x-wcc-keys" (child names) and "x-wcc-more" (the call that expands them), so answers stay small.
Use it to look up the exact option names, types, enums and defaults before writing a spec, instead of guessing. Ask for the narrowest path you need; do not fetch the whole tree at high depth. Unknown paths fail with kind "not_found" and a did-you-mean hint.
Read-only.
Examples: {"path": "plotOptions.radialColumn"}, {"path": "xaxis.labels", "depth": 1}, {} for the top-level keys.

path.description: Dotted option path, e.g. 'plotOptions.bar' or 'chart.toolbar'. Omit for the root.

depth.description: Levels of nested properties to expand. Default 2; 0 returns only the node itself with its child keys.

tools.name: list_chart_types
tools.title: List chart types
tools.description:
List every chart type this server can render with its tier (premium true/false) and, for premium layers, the module that provides it.
Use it to pick a valid chart.type, or to find a free alternative when a premium type fails with kind "license". Read-only, no arguments.

tools.name: list_examples
tools.title: List curated examples

type.description: Only examples of this chart.type, e.g. 'line'.

query.description: Case-insensitive words that must all appear in id or title.

premium.description: true = only premium, false = only free examples.

tools.title: Get example spec

resourceTemplates.name: docs
resourceTemplates.title: West Coast Charts documentation
resourceTemplates.description: Library guide, option reference and feature docs as markdown. Large pages (options reference) can exceed 50k tokens; prefer get_schema for single options.

resourceTemplates.name: renders
resourceTemplates.title: Recent renders
resourceTemplates.description: The last 32 outputs of render_chart in this session (SVG text or PNG blob), addressed by the uri render_chart returned.

prompts.name: build_dashboard
prompts.title: Build a dashboard
prompts.description: Plan and build a multi-chart West Coast Charts dashboard for a goal, validating and verifying every chart.

arguments.name: goal
arguments.description: What the dashboard must let someone see or decide, e.g. "ops control room for 3 clusters"

arguments.name: data
arguments.description: Description or sample of the available data (fields, units, granularity)

prompts.name: pick_chart_type
prompts.title: Pick a chart type for data
prompts.description: Recommend the best West Coast Charts type for a dataset and question, with a validated starter spec.

arguments.name: data
arguments.description: The data: fields, units, number of series/categories/points, or a small sample

arguments.name: question
arguments.description: What the reader should learn, e.g. "which region is slowest"
